# gzip-encoding twins — committed byte-exact

Two pairs live here. Both prove that **the same VRML text can be a legal gzip
`.wrl` at wildly different sizes**; they differ in what they say about the Mall
upload ceiling of **80 KiB = `80 * 1024` = 81,920 bytes**.

## Pair 1 — encoding variance

| file | bytes | role |
|---|---:|---|
| `twin.plain.wrl` | 81,753 | the decompressed text both archives contain |
| `twin-small.wrl.gz` | 451 | DEFLATE level 9 — **PASS** (under 81,920 B) |
| `twin-large.wrl.gz` | 81,781 | DEFLATE level 0 (stored) — **also PASS** (under 81,920 B) |

A ~181× difference in measured bytes from identical text, which is exactly why a
predicted repack size can never stand in for the size of the file that will
actually be uploaded.

`twin-large.wrl.gz` is **not** an over-limit artifact. It was created when the
limit was wrongly recorded as 81,290 B; under the correct 81,920 B ceiling it
passes with 139 B to spare. Do not describe it as exceeding the limit.

## Pair 2 — limit straddle

| file | bytes | role |
|---|---:|---|
| `limit-twin.plain.wrl` | 120,030 | the decompressed text both archives contain |
| `limit-twin-small.wrl.gz` | 589 | DEFLATE level 9 — **PASS** (81,331 B under the limit) |
| `limit-twin-large.wrl.gz` | 120,063 | DEFLATE level 0 (stored) — **FAIL** (38,143 B over) |

This is the pair that proves the gate: identical text, one artifact each side of
81,920 B, with a comfortable deterministic margin rather than a fragile
one-byte difference.

## Provenance and byte contract

Generated once with Node `zlib.gzipSync` at levels 9 and 0, with the gzip OS
byte forced to `0x03` and the mtime field left at 0 so the bytes are stable.
**They are committed as exact bytes and must never be regenerated by a test** —
a test that rebuilds its own oracle proves nothing. `test/fixtures/** -text` in
the root `.gitattributes` keeps Git for Windows from rewriting them, and
`test/preview/fixture-byte-contract.test.js` pins every file's byte count and
SHA-256.
